doc.title: Eddie Locke interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, NY, January 13, 2001

chapter: Detroit and the Bop and Locke act
title: The Bop and Locke drummer and tap-dance act
summary: Locke describes the song-and-dance drumming act, modelled on Red and Curly, rehearsed two years with help from Tommy Flanagan and Pepper Adams.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Tell me about Bop and Locke.
Well, did you ever hear of Red and Curly?

They used to travel with Lionel Hampton. But the first time I saw them they were with Erskine Hawkin’s band. They had a drummer act like that. And they were tap dancers. They were basically tap dancers. Ours was the exact opposite. We were drummers and jive tap dancers. But we did this all ourself you know, and I think we must be the — we rehearsed for about two years putting this act together. And Tommy Flanagan and all the guys used to accompany us and help us. Pepper Adams, they’d put bands together and play our music for us you know. That’s the way the guys were in Detroit. And we decided we were going to try to make it with this act. And we probably would have been better but it was at a bad time, when we got that act together, that’s when Vaudeville was dying. That’s when Rock ‘n Roll came. That’s when all the tap dancers and everything went like kaput.
